topic: Advanced Machine Learning and Ensemble Methods
learningObjectives: Understand decision trees and ensemble learning concepts.
Identify suitable ensemble methods for machine learning tasks.

activities.title: Anatomy of a Decision Tree
activities.instruction: Explore the main components of a decision tree.

content.concept: Decision trees make predictions by recursively splitting data according to conditions on input features.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The starting point of the decision tree containing the first split.
A node where a feature-based condition determines the next path.
A connection representing the outcome of a decision.
A terminal node where the tree produces a final prediction.
The class or numerical value produced at a leaf.

activities.title: Build a Random Forest
activities.instruction: Assemble the components of a random forest ensemble.

content.concept: Random forests combine many decision trees trained with randomized data and feature selections, then aggregate their predictions.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Compare Ensemble Strategies
activities.instruction: Identify the core idea behind each ensemble strategy.

content.concept: Bagging trains models independently on varied samples and combines their predictions, while boosting builds models sequentially to focus on previous errors.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Bagging → Train multiple models independently and aggregate predictions
Boosting → Train models sequentially while focusing on previous errors
Random Forest → Ensemble of randomized decision trees
Gradient Boosting → Sequentially build models that improve the current ensemble
config.answer: Bagging → Train multiple models independently and aggregate predictions

activities.title: Tune Tree Complexity
activities.instruction: Adjust tree depth and observe how model complexity can affect learning behavior.

content.concept: Increasing tree depth can allow a decision tree to capture more detailed patterns but may also increase the risk of overfitting.
